title: Introduce tenant KMS obligation mapper and audit normalizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add tenant-level KMS obligation mapping and an audit-normalizer pipeline. No public API changes. Operational flag gate and automated migration helper included.
description:
Context & motivation: Customers with regional compliance requirements ask for stronger guarantees that KMS usage and operator RBAC decisions are evaluated against tenant-specific obligations (e.g., allowed provider list, region pinning). Existing enforcement paths were scattered: some checks lived in the KMS allocator, some in the policy-enforcer, and audit records varied by component, making post-hoc compliance proofs brittle. This PR introduces a centralized Tenant KMS Obligation Mapper (TKOM) plus an Audit Normalizer that standardizes provenance metadata across services. Goal: make decisions deterministic, auditable, and easier to reason about during audits without large surface-area changes to runtime.

Summary of changes: Implements TKOM service/interface (inference and private branches) that consumes tenant profiles and compiles a normalized obligations object (allowed_providers, region_pin, soft_restrictions). Adds an enforcement shim used by the KMS allocator and policy-enforcer that consults TKOM results. Introduces an audit-normalizer pipeline that transforms existing audit events into a canonical schema with KMS_obligation_id, decision_reason, and operator_scope fields. Adds a lightweight migration assistant that backfills obligation IDs for existing tenants and a feature-flag to gate rollout.

Checklist (implemented): - Add TKOM API + in-memory cache with TTL and refresh metrics. - Integrate shim into kms-allocator and policy-enforcer with fallbacks. - Audit normalizer: schema, transformer, and retention hooks. - Migration assistant: dry-run mode + backfill. - Feature flag: config.features.tk_obligation_mapper (off by default) - Unit + integration tests for policy-enforcer and audit pipeline. - Security review and threat model update.

Commits (high level): - 3d8a9f2: bootstrap tenant obligation mapper service and core types. - b7f21c1: add cache adapter + metrics and config toggles. - a12f4e7: integrate enforcement shim into kms-allocator (use obligation id and provider whitelist). - f9e2b33: audit-normalizer transformer + schema migration and tests. - c1b4d0a: migration assistant and dry-run tooling. - 4b7c9ae: docs, rollout playbook, and e2e tests for private deployer.

Changed areas/files (high level): - services/tkom/* (new service, API, cache, tests) - services/kms-allocator/shim.go (enforcement shim and integrations) - services/policy-enforcer/obligation_adapter.go (adapter to consult TKOM) - observability/audit/normalizer/* (transformer, schema v2) - infra/feature-flags.yaml (feature gating) - tools/migration-assistant/* (backfill + dry-run) - docs/security/tkom.md and runbook/rollout-tkom.md

Testing & CI: Initial CI run showed a flaky integration test in policy-enforcer (race on cache refresh). Fixed by adding a mutex and a retry backoff (commits b7f21c1 -> a12f4e7). Final CI: linux-unit (pass), linux-integration (pass after rerun), lint (pass), go-vet (pass). Performance: obligation lookup latency added ~0.9ms median when cache cold; negligible when warm. Measured end-to-end add of ~1-2ms tail for KMS allocation path in our perf-canary harness under synthetic load. Included microbenchmarks in services/tkom/bench.

Backward compatibility & migration: Feature-gated rollout with migration assistant to compute obligation ids and validate no tenants are left without obligations. Default behaviour when feature off: system behaves as today. When on: enforcement shim treats unknown obligation as permissive (configurable) for a 48h soft-enforcement window, then strict. Migration assistant dry-run produced no tenants that would move to strict deny in our staging sample.

Security review & threat model: Conducted with Priya Raman. Major findings: ensure TKOM caches don't leak cross-tenant data; we added tenant-scoped cache keys and telemetry scrubbing. Audit-normalizer includes hashed operator identifiers to support non-repudiation while minimizing PII in long-term retention. Threat mitigations and design notes are in docs/security/tkom.md.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy TKOM in staging with feature flag off. 2) Run migration assistant dry-run and reconcile. 3) Enable feature for internal tenants (canary). 4) Monitor metrics (obligation_hits, obligation_misses, audit_normalizer_errors) and SLOs for KMS latency. 5) Expand to >80% tenants, then strict enforcement after 48h window. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and flush caches.

Follow-ups: - Formal evaluation to surface obligation diffs in Console (ENG-5378). - Add per-operator attribute mapping to aid operator-scoped RBAC (design doc linked). - Consider moving obligation compilation into policy-compiler for offline verification.

review_comments: Jared Alvarez: Can you clarify the fallback semantics if TKOM is unavailable? The PR description says permissive by default but the code reads as strict in one path.

Maya Chen (reply): Good catch. Updated the shim logic to centralize fallback semantics in shim.go and added unit tests. Permissive by default is now enforced via config.features.tk_obligation_mapper.default_mode.
Priya Raman: Please add a note to the threat model about cache key entropy and operator identifier hashing.
Maya Chen (reply): Added section in docs/security/tkom.md and a short unit test that verifies operator id hashing is stable across restarts.
Eleanor Wu: Audit normalizer should include a version field to allow roll-forward parsing; add schema v2 header.
Maya Chen (reply): Included schema_version on all normalized events and migration tooling to backfill older records.

notes: Operational: Monitor obligation_miss_rate and audit_normalizer_errors closely for first 72h.
Performance: Expect up to 2ms added tail latency on KMS allocation when cache cold; warm cache negligible.
Compliance: This change centralizes obligation decisioning to simplify SOC2 evidence collection.
